expectations.text: Recommends against building the MCP server this quarter, parking it until agent-demand signals (RFPs requiring MCP compatibility, or observed agent traffic) appear
expectations.evidence: "Don't ship an MCP server this quarter." The Q1 trigger is "one RFP or security review requiring MCP, or 3+ customers asking in writing, or agent traffic above 1% of calls".

expectations.text: Names the absence of agent signals (zero agent traffic, no customer asks) as the reason MCP is parked, rather than arguing only from team effort or generic prioritization
expectations.evidence: "Agent demand: none. Logs show zero agent traffic and no customer has asked about MCP. This leaves MCP parked."

expectations.text: Identifies fixing the drifting OpenAPI spec as a prerequisite scheduled before any derived surface (SDKs, MCP, generated docs) enters the plan
expectations.evidence: "A drifting spec gets fixed before any derived surface is scheduled." Derivation gate: nothing derived before the week-6 contract-stable declaration.

expectations.text: States that when MCP is eventually built it must be derived or generated from the existing API contract, never hand-built as a separate product
expectations.evidence: "Generated from the verified spec"; "every platform that shipped MCP generated it over an existing API."

expectations.text: Flags the 60% API coverage as a shallow-API-first failure: partners discover mid-integration that later steps still need manual touches, so depth is probed per capability
expectations.evidence: "a 60% API means customers finish integrations and then hit a UI-only step... probe each capability and list which flows can't be completed end to end."

expectations.text: Sequences REST completion plus webhooks as the first surfaces, noting webhooks ride the same infrastructure rather than opening a new paradigm
expectations.evidence: REST coverage and webhooks are scheduled in Q4, but the plan never says webhooks ride the same infrastructure rather than opening a new paradigm.

expectations.text: Labels the per-call agent monetization idea speculative, noting unproven unit economics and that observed per-call volumes are tiny and partly wash-traded
expectations.evidence: It says "Label it speculative" and that x402 volumes "collapsed after peaking". It never mentions tiny volumes or wash trading.

expectations.text: Caps concurrent new-surface builds at the stated two-engineer capacity, sequencing surfaces one at a time
expectations.evidence: "Concurrency gate: at most one new surface runs at a time. Webhooks occupy the slot in Q4."

expectations.text: Includes review triggers that reopen the plan early, among them agent-demand signals moving from none to present
expectations.evidence: "An agent-demand signal appears (RFP, written asks, agent traffic)."

expectations.text: Justifies delaying higher-abstraction surfaces via the dependency mechanism (Hyrum's Law or equivalent: once enough consumers depend on observable behavior, the contract is near-impossible to change)
expectations.evidence: It says "MCP and SDKs presuppose a stable contract" and "retrofitting one later is the expensive direction", but never explains the mechanism of consumers depending on observable behavior.
